rv.q: Restrained, polite and somewhat miscast production of Shakespeare’s tragedy
It’s a tragedy shaped as much by complicity as intent, and this staging’s greatest strength lies in how recognisably human the roots of evil feel.

The battle scenes are thrillingly dangerous, with staves flying around perilously close to front-row spectators at times, as the actors whirl and flail in fights carefully choreographed by Annie Mackenzie.

cn.t: Tobacco Factory's ensemble-driven Macbeth earns praise for shifting focus from the doomed hero to those who enable his rise and fall, with judicious editing tightening Shakespeare's already compact tragedy.
